'''Theron Nett''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] from [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] who later became a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], and [[Wingmate/Legends|wingman]] of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron's]] leader, [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]], during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

==Biography==
Prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Theron Nett worked for years as a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], a career he considered himself lucky to have survived. Nett joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Dantooine Squadron]], with squadron leader [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]] serving as his mentor and frequent [[Wingmate/Legends|wingman]]. Later transferred to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], he struck up a friendship with his squadmate [[Nozzo Naytaan/Legends|Nozzo Naytaan]], a young [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] whose excessive recklessness he sought to curb.<ref name="EGTW" />

Joined by [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-X2/Legends|R2-X2]], Nett flew a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] as [[Red Ten/Legends|Red Ten]] in the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]], once again flying on [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]] Dreis' wing during the second attack run on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. Attempting to cover the squadron leader from the pursuing [[Black Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Black Squadron]], he was shot down and killed by [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] [[TIE pilot|pilot]] "[[DS-61-3|Backstabber]]."<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|There's too much interference.|Theron Nett|<ref name="ANH" />}}
Theron Nett was played by English actor [[Robert O'Mahoney]], who is uncredited, although he has just as many lines as [[Garrick Hagon]] or [[William Hootkins]] and any of the other minor pilot actors who were credited.<ref name="SWA">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsaficionado|url=2012/06/aficionado-classic-blog-lost-pilot.html|name=FBTB.net|text=SDCC - The LEGO Star Wars Minifigure Gallery}}</ref> The depiction of "Theron's" death strangely shows him with the helmet worn by [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. This is in fact footage of a different actor, [[Chris Matthews|Christopher Matthews]], intended to be [[Red Twelve/Legends|Red Twelve]] (later identified as [[Puck Naeco/Legends|Puck Naeco]]), whose fighter is destroyed moments before.<ref name="Notes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10}}</ref>

An X-wing pilot figure depicting Nett's helmet design in a [[2014]] [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] set was identified as Theron Nett in a display at that year's San Diego Comic Con.<ref name="FBTB">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fbtb.net/lego-star-wars/2014/07/24/sdcc-the-lego-star-wars-minifigure-gallery|text=SDCC - The LEGO Star Wars Minifigure Gallery|work=FBTB.net|archivedate=20200929031301}}</ref>
